context.body: Poetry and prophecy preserve confession, complaint, praise, warning, withheld pardon, restored relation, remembered sin, and promised forgiveness without flattening each speaker. The bounded source is Jeremiah 36:1–8.

payload.posture: Read Jeremiah 36:1–8 as prayer, praise, and prophetic speech evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The passage gives bounded Forgiveness evidence, but it does not make this request, response, condition, means, or outcome a universal procedure: The scroll is written and read so Judah may hear, turn from evil, and receive forgiveness of iniquity and sin.
payload.title: The scroll is read in hope of turning and forgiveness
